newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on corn/soy decline.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on corn/soy decline.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower, pulled down by a drop in corn and soybean futures, traders said.
Forecasts for rain later in the week in the U.S. Midwest knocked CBOT corn and soybeans lower after a higher opening, they said.
LIT America sold five million bushels of December SRW wheat, Rosenthal Collins sold 4.5 million December and Term Commodities sold three million December, traders said.
Dry weather in portions of Australia's wheat growing region and in portions of Canada's grain belt may have provided some underpinning.

The Australian Wheat Board Monday cut its estimate of Australia's 1997-98 wheat crop by one million tonnes to between 14 million and 15 million tonnes. AWB general manager for merchandising Ron Storey said the AWB could expect to have a 10 million- to 11-million-tonne export programme against the 18-million-tonne program of 1996-97.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 4-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down 6-3/4 at $3.54-3/4 per bushel. December closed seven cents lower at $3.69-1/2.
USDA's weekly export inspections report Monday showed wheat inspected for export during the week ended July 31 at 24.009 million bushels, above expectations for 18 million to 22 million bushels.
Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report held no surprises for the market, traders said.
The CFTC said as of Tuesday, non-commercials were long wheat by roughly 95.0 million bushels and short by 72.57 million. Commercials were long by 204.0 million bushels and short by 275.2 million.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 27,000 contracts, above the 18,733 traded Friday.

In wheat options, Refco Inc sold 400 December $3.80 calls at 17-1/2 cents, Lind Waldock sold 100 December $3.80 calls at 18 cents, Smith Barney bought 300 December $3.70 puts at 19 cents and sold 300 December $3.60 puts at 14 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, below the 6,555 traded Friday.
